evidence.note: Recomputed accurate decoded-byte bpb (~1.028) instead of trusting the script's optimistic 4-bytes/token estimate, correctly diagnosed the run as above target, and launched a directed continuation rather than resubmitting.
Diagnosed that resume LR 6e-4 worsened validation as too aggressive after quantized load; interrupted and restarted at 1e-4 — a reasoned single-lever correction with re-check.

After plateau, systematically falsified levers (temperature scale already optimal, bigram/trigram worsen) and trained a deeper 12-layer model, tracking it against the 9-layer baseline and abandoning it when evidence showed no gain.
Traded the quantization scheme (int4 packing) to buy capacity for a 52M model within the byte cap — direct capacity-vs-quant frontier reasoning — then abandoned it on evidence it stayed behind.

Treated the size↔bpb frontier as the optimization object: escalated load-time n-gram interpolation (5→6→7-gram) with zero checkpoint cost, each experiment updating the design, crossing threshold; caught and fixed an off-by-one bug to land at 0.98164.

reasoning: The agent consistently diagnosed WHY each run missed (optimistic bpb accounting, over-aggressive LR, capacity plateau, quant loss) and changed the right lever, matching the level-8 anchor of adapting design to the binding constraint (e.g. int4 to buy capacity). It further treated the frontier as the object of optimization, compounding falsified runs into a size-free n-gram scheme that crossed the target — the level-10 behavior — but let some clearly-behind experiments run longer than needed and finished with thin headroom, so I place it at 9.
